hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to a single, elongated, cylindrical or rod-like object oriented diagonally from the upper left to the lower right. The activating feature is characterized by high contrast, presenting as a dark form—typically black, dark brown, deep reddish-brown, or metallic blue—against a uniform, light-colored background of grey, beige, or off-white. The object typically spans the majority of the frame's diagonal, appearing as a dominant central line or shaft, such as a pen, wooden stick, flute, insect body, or reptile. The feature typically occupies a central band roughly 10–30% of the image width while traversing 50–100% of the frame's length. The neuron remains invariant to the object's semantic identity, material properties (wood, metal, organic), and surface texture, provided the strong diagonal linearity and dark-on-light contrast are maintained.

The lighting is diffuse and originates from behind the subject, rendering the wing membranes luminous and semi-transparent while casting the skeletal veins and body in high-contrast silhouette against the lighter field.

Centering the composition and angled diagonally from the upper left to the lower right is the mid-section of a handcrafted wooden flute, resting on a textured, neutral grey fabric surface. The flute is constructed from contrasting woods: the main body is a smooth, dark chocolate-brown wood, while the top face features a lighter, golden-yellow wood with a distinctive quilted or rippled grain pattern that shimmers slightly under the light. A thin, bright turquoise inlay strip runs along the seam between the dark and light woods, providing a sharp visual border. Drilled into the lighter wood face are four visible circular finger holes, aligned in a row along the instrument's length. The interior of these holes is pitch black. The surface around each hole is gently scalloped or concave, creating smooth depressions in the wood. The lighting is soft and diffuse, casting a gentle sheen on the polished wood surfaces and highlighting the depth of the grain, particularly on the golden section. The background is a mottled grey, resembling a tight-knit carpet or felt, which is slightly out of focus compared to the sharp detail of the flute's finger holes and wood grain. The flute dominates the frame, occupying a central band that spans roughly half the width of the visible area, leaving triangular sections of the grey background in the upper right and lower left corners.

A close-up, slightly high-angle view captures a segment of a car wheel and tire, oriented diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. The left side of the image is dominated by the dark grey, glossy rubber of the tire tread, which appears slightly wet. The tread pattern consists of a column of angled, rectangular shoulder blocks on the far left, separated by deep, dark lateral grooves. Tiny, hair-like rubber molding vents, or "whiskers," protrude vertically from the smooth surfaces of the tread blocks. Embossed upside-down on the sidewall is the alphanumeric sequence "225/40" followed by "Z", indicating tire specifications, located near the top center of the visible tire area. Below this text, a distinct, small yellow circular dot is painted on the black rubber near the bead. The right side of the composition features a portion of a silver alloy wheel rim. The rim's outer lip is a bright, curved metallic band that meets the tire. Inside the lip, parts of two thick, silver spokes are visible, framing dark, triangular voids that reveal the shadowed, black interior of the wheel barrel. The silver surface is smooth and reflective, contrasting with the textured rubber. On the extreme left edge, distinct blades of green grass are visible against a dark background, suggesting the wheel is resting on a lawn. The lighting creates specular highlights on the wet tire tread and soft gradients on the curved silver spokes.

The shaft is primarily a deep reddish-brown color and features a prominent, raised lattice texture resembling leather wrapping or carved wood, where lighter brown strips crisscross over a darker underlying surface to form a repeating pattern of diamonds down the length of the handle. At the top left, the wood appears to rest against or emerge from close proximity to the fur, while a soft, dark shadow is cast on the concrete surface immediately to the left of the stick, running parallel to it, suggesting a light source positioned to the upper right.

A section of a dark-scaled snake's body dominates the vertical center of the view, curving gently from the bottom right towards the top center. The lighting is soft and diffuse, casting minimal shadows but highlighting the texture of the snake's scales and the roughness of the ground.
